reference: There is no equivalent GNU CLI for this shell builtin's set/current/validate verbs: GNU locale reports process locale information through a different interface. Contract expectations below use the builtin's help text and documented accepted names, Bash type/help behavior, and POSIX locale environment precedence (LC_ALL, then LC_<category>, then LANG; default C). No expectation is derived from the candidate's output.
coverage: Bash builtin availability and documented help metadata
validate accepts the documented C, POSIX, and C.UTF-8 names and rejects an unsupported locale
current output for all named categories under the C fallback
current resolution of LC_ALL, a category variable, and LANG fallback
set updates a category and set ALL takes precedence over individual categories
exclusions: GNU locale is not a matching oracle for this custom shell API, so there are no parity cases.
Only C, POSIX, and C.UTF-8 contract values are exercised; locale database behavior beyond those names is not qualified.
End-to-end effects on a locale-sensitive child process are deferred because this fixture environment fixes the inherited locale to C and provides no dedicated independent libc probe.

cases.purpose: Bash type/help metadata must identify locale as a builtin and advertise the documented verbs and supported locale names.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t locale) == builtin ]] || exit 1
help_text=$(help locale)
[[ $help_text == *"Minimal LC_* environment plumbing for bash-os."* ]] || exit 1
[[ $help_text == *"locale set CATEGORY VALUE"* ]] || exit 1
[[ $help_text == *"locale current"* ]] || exit 1
[[ $help_text == *"locale validate VALUE"* ]] || exit 1
[[ $help_text == *"Recognized locale values: C, POSIX, C.UTF-8."* ]] || exit 1
printf 'builtin\nhelp-contract-ok\n'

cases.purpose: The documented locale names C, POSIX, and C.UTF-8 are accepted by validate.
cases.script:
locale validate C
locale validate POSIX
locale validate C.UTF-8
printf 'accepted=3\n'

cases.purpose: The builtin help says names other than C, POSIX, and C.UTF-8 are rejected.
validate without its required VALUE operand is a usage error.
With LC_ALL unset and LANG=C, current reports the effective C locale for each advertised category and LANG.
cases.script:
unset LC_ALL
export LANG=C
locale current
cases.stdout:
LC_ALL=C
LC_CTYPE=C
LC_NUMERIC=C
LC_TIME=C
LC_COLLATE=C
LC_MONETARY=C
LC_MESSAGES=C
LC_PAPER=C
LC_NAME=C
LC_ADDRESS=C
LC_TELEPHONE=C
LC_MEASUREMENT=C
LC_IDENTIFICATION=C
LANG=C

cases.purpose: Without LC_ALL, a set LC_NUMERIC wins for that category while other categories and LANG fall back to LANG.
cases.script:
unset LC_ALL
export LANG=POSIX LC_NUMERIC=C
locale current NUMERIC
locale current CTYPE
locale current LANG

cases.purpose: LC_ALL overrides both a category-specific variable and LANG when current resolves an effective category or LANG.
cases.script:
export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 LC_NUMERIC=C LANG=POSIX
locale current LC_NUMERIC
locale current LANG

cases.purpose: set accepts a documented category/value pair, updates the shell variable, and current reports the new category value.
cases.script:
unset LC_ALL LC_CTYPE
export LANG=POSIX
locale set LC_CTYPE C.UTF-8
[[ ${LC_CTYPE-} == C.UTF-8 ]] || exit 1
locale current LC_CTYPE

cases.purpose: set ALL updates LC_ALL while preserving category variables; current resolves the selected category through LC_ALL.
cases.script:
unset LC_ALL
export LANG=POSIX LC_CTYPE=C.UTF-8 LC_NUMERIC=C
locale set ALL POSIX
[[ ${LC_ALL-} == POSIX ]] || exit 1
[[ ${LC_CTYPE-} == C.UTF-8 && ${LC_NUMERIC-} == C ]] || exit 1
locale current LC_NUMERIC

cases.purpose: set rejects an unrecognized LC category with a usage status and diagnostic.
An unrecognized verb is reported as a usage error.
Verify that variables set by the builtin produce the intended behavior in a locale-sensitive child process, separately from this builtin's environment-plumbing contract.
